target.name: ByteCodeInterpreter VM value effect (sub_08004380)
target.role: set one bit of a byte array inside an object, from the value the VM popped
target.notes: sub_08004380, 22 bytes and 11 instructions, one terminator at 0x08004394, no branches, NO calls and NO literal pool. A LEAF, so the effect is established by this routine alone and no helper had to be followed. Its argument contract is already proven from its caller: native dispatch entry 29 passes r0 = *(0x08054FBC + 0x14) and r1 = values[count-1] popped from the VM stack. THE CONCRETE EFFECT: it sets bit (value & 7) of the byte at base + (value >> 3) + 0x55, preserving the other seven bits. The two shifts are the standard bit-array split - `asrs r2, r1, #3` selects the byte, `lsls r3, r1, #0x1d` then `lsrs r3, r3, #0x1d` isolates the low three bits to select the bit within it - and `orrs` plus `strb` make it a read-modify-write. THE BYTE-INDEX SHIFT IS ARITHMETIC, which matters: a value with bit 31 set gives a negative byte index and the write lands BEFORE the base. 0xFFFFFFFF maps to base + 0x54 bit 7, one byte before its unsigned position, and 0x80000000 maps to base + 0xF0000055, nowhere near the logical-shift answer of base + 0x10000055. THE RECONSTRUCTION MODELS THE ARITHMETIC SHIFT EXPLICITLY because C's right shift of a negative signed value is implementation-defined. THERE IS NO BOUNDS CHECK and no NULL check: no compare against a size and no conditional branch exists anywhere in the routine, so every value selects a byte and that byte is written, however far outside the object it lies. No guard was added. UNKNOWN: what the bit MEANS, how large the byte array is, and what reads the bit afterwards. No name is assigned to the object, the array or the bit, and nothing is imported from another title.

comparison.match_claim_note: MEASUREMENT ONLY. This compares a modern GCC build against the cartridge. A modern compiler is not the original compiler, so a difference here is expected and proves nothing; an identity here would also prove nothing about ADS 1.2. ADS_MATCH stays BLOCKED.
